p01.why: A class-type argument can be a braced list, and equal members give one specialization.

p02.why: The pack takes the arguments after the first, zero or two.

p03.why: 5 for a const int& parameter would bind the reference to a temporary.

p04.why: Class arguments are copy-initialized, from a braced list or through the int constructor.

p05.why: Constant and template template packs take zero or more arguments.

p06.why: The address of an automatic variable is not a valid pointer argument.

p07.why: The definition outside the class uses its own head, which has no default, so C<> lacks an argument; the check happens at the definition.

p08.why: With an argument list the inherited injected name names the template, so Base<long> is valid.

p09.why: A double constant is a valid argument for a double parameter.

p10.why: A variable template name needs an argument list.

p11.why: Qualified names that find templates open argument lists.

p12.why: Equal values, aliases replaced, and defaults added give the same specializations; const int differs.

p13.why: int() as a type argument is the function type, not a pointer.

p14.why: A placeholder parameter in either head matches any type in the other; 'a' converts to int 97.

p15.why: The member template name before < opens a list, and the call gives the rest.

p16.why: A default can use an earlier parameter, and <> takes every default.

p17.why: The injected name alone is the current specialization; with arguments it names the template.

p18.why: U has no argument and no default.

p19.why: Enumerators of equal value are the same; unions compare by active member; array members compare element by element.

p20.why: The reference member would bind to a subobject of a temporary.

p21.why: An enumerator of another scoped enumeration needs an explicit conversion.

p22.why: int* to void* is not an allowed conversion for a pointer argument.

p23.why: 1.5 is a double and does not convert to float for a constant argument.

p24.why: A head with a pack accepts a template with any number of type parameters.

p25.why: Base alone in Both is ambiguous between two injected class names, also as a template template argument.

p26.why: count is not a constant expression.

p27.why: A string literal is not valid for a pointer parameter.

p28.why: Pointer arguments compare by entity; a reference variable with a constant initializer names its object.

p29.why: Member lookup in Gauge finds the data member v, so the < is less-than and count(bool,bool) is chosen.

p30.why: A scoped enumerator does not convert to int implicitly.

p31.why: identity has one template parameter and two arguments are given.

p32.why: int() is read as a type, which is not valid for a constant parameter; EDG differs (Q-0170) but the rule gives reject.

p34.why: As a template template argument the injected name names the template Node.

p35.why: Defaults fill in, and U's default uses T.

p36.why: A class is not a valid argument for a template template parameter.

p37.why: With a leading pack, the pack takes every explicit argument and x is deduced; with no pack, long goes to the invented parameter.

p38.why: With T = int&, T* is a pointer to reference, which is not valid.

p39.why: A pass-through alias template is a different template, so the two types differ; GCC and EDG differ (Q-0168).

p40.why: A qualified name never finds the injected class name, so lib::Box needs an argument list.

p41.why: Lookup finds nothing or only a function, so < opens a list and ADL finds lib::pick both times.

p42.why: In use() the local v hides the template so < is less-than; at namespace scope v<1, 2> is the variable template, 3.

p43.why: Pair's second parameter has no default and no match in a one-parameter head.

p44.why: Arguments match parameters by position and kind.

p45.why: All are addresses of static-storage objects or functions or null; the static const in address() is usable in constant expressions.

p46.why: An alias template is a valid template template argument.

p47.why: An integer does not convert to double for a constant argument.

p48.why: Hidden is private where the argument is written.

p49.why: Too many arguments for a template with no pack.

p50.why: An overloaded name selects the overload of the parameter's function type.

p51.why: The > of a named cast and >> of nested lists are nested and do not end the list.

p52.why: The >> operator ends the list without parentheses.

p53.why: Array to pointer plus qualification, function to pointer, noexcept dropped, and nullptr are all allowed.

p54.why: A concept is not valid for a template template parameter.

p55.why: Derived* to Base* is a conversion to a base, not allowed.

p56.why: ListAlias is a different template from List, so the explicit specialization does not apply and value is 0; GCC and EDG differ (Q-0168).

p57.why: Two unions with no active member are one specialization; GCC rejects the value (Q-0117).

p58.why: Parenthesized > and >> stay in the list; >> closes two nested lists.

p59.why: Leading arguments are explicit; T is deduced and U takes its default.

p60.why: A class template name with no list must not be part of a pointer declarator.

p61.why: Function and variable template-ids work as written.

p62.why: The parameter Size hides the template so < is less-than; at namespace scope Size<3, 4> is a template-id.

p63.why: Any type is valid for a type parameter, including function, array of unknown bound, reference, and lambda closure types.

p64.why: An argument template can have extra parameters with defaults.

p65.why: The > ends the list, and the rest does not parse.

p66.why: float to double is not allowed even when exact.

p67.why: An integer does not convert to a scoped enumeration implicitly.

p68.why: A use of the parameter selects the argument template's partial specializations.

p69.why: The address of __func__ is not a valid argument.

p70.why: A variable template is not valid for a template template parameter that takes a class template.

p71.why: A type is not valid for a constant parameter.

p72.why: Promotions, unscoped enumeration conversion, and a constexpr user-defined conversion are allowed; Num<'a'> is Num<97>.

p73.why: Local, unnamed, and incomplete classes and unnamed enumerations are valid type arguments.

p74.why: Owner can name its own private member in an argument.

p75.why: int::size_type is not valid in the later parameter's type.

p77.why: Num's parameter is a constant parameter and the head wants a type parameter.

p78.why: 2.0 to int converts between floating-point and integer.

p79.why: A string literal copy-initializes a class with a const char* constructor.

p81.why: In an explicit or partial specialization the injected name names that specialization.

p82.why: 0.5 and 1.0/2 have one representation; 0.0 and -0.0 differ.

p83.why: An alias that changes its argument is a different template, and PtrList<int> is List<int*>.

p84.why: Head arguments of int convert to long, so the fixed types match; Clang 18 and EDG differ (Q-0201).

p85.why: Lookup of pick in the template finds nothing, so < opens a list and ADL finds lib::pick at instantiation.

p86.why: Base alone is ambiguous between the two injected class names.

p87.why: The integer 0 does not convert to a pointer here.

p88.why: The template gets no access to Owner's private Hidden.

p89.why: IsIntegral is a class template; the fold gives true then false.

p90.why: A member or array element of a static object is a valid pointer argument.

p91.why: Even with defaults, the name without a list must not be part of a pointer declarator.

p92.why: An expression is not valid for a type parameter.

p93.why: Reference arguments name static objects; bump changes counter twice.
